title: Procedural Yellow Sponge Volume
weighting_note: This is a material exercise on a native cube. Eighty points assess volumetric material structure, appearance, transport, and independent controls. No geometry-generation credit is assigned to the container or procedural shader. Scene composition receives ten points for the useful transmission comparison; reproducible delivery receives ten.

rubric.criterion: The visible cube has an editable, fully procedural three-dimensional density field that produces its internal porous volume without external texture or volume assets.

scoring_rule.PASS: The assigned material produces spatially varying density throughout all three dimensions of the cube, including the interior; the cube remains an editable container and the material has no image-texture, imported-volume, or external-asset dependency.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: A material assigned to the cube renders an actual volume with spatially varying density in at least one dimension, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: There is no assigned spatially varying volume material on a visible cube. A uniform volume, surface-only shading or displacement, flat alpha pattern, or image of a sponge alone is below the minimum.

verification.method: material inspection and controlled interior renders
verification.procedure: Inspect the material actually assigned to the cube and its data dependencies. In a temporary scene copy, compare three orthogonal thin interior slices of the same density field, using native test containers if needed, and inspect variation away from the original boundary. Confirm that the effect is generated by the volume material and that the original container remains editable. Do not require a particular node recipe.

rubric.criterion: The saved default has a dense, fine-pored sponge appearance with irregular small voids and a retained cubic silhouette.

scoring_rule.PASS: Fine irregular pores are distributed across the visible body and are evident near its boundaries; they are small relative to a cube edge, the cubic silhouette remains clear, and the material avoids broad voids, conspicuous stretching, and featureless regions. Pore detail remains identifiable after render noise has converged.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: At least one substantial visible face of an existing sponge volume shows a genuine repeated pore pattern that survives converged rendering, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: No substantial visible face of an existing volume shows a genuine repeated pore pattern after convergence. Sampling grain alone, a featureless volume, or a few isolated cavities is below the minimum.

verification.method: controlled render and visual material inspection
verification.procedure: Render the saved default from the submission camera and a close view of an existing face and edge. Repeat with increased sampling until random noise stops changing the material reading. Inspect pore distribution, relative cell size, boundary character, and directional distortion; do not count viewport grain as structure.

rubric.criterion: The existing sponge body has saturated warm yellow coloration with shaded depth rather than flat emission.

scoring_rule.PASS: The body's brighter and darker substantial regions both read as warm yellow under neutral illumination; saturation survives the shading, and depth and shadow variation remain visible without a flat emissive appearance.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: An existing substantial region of the sponge body reads as yellow under neutral illumination, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: No existing substantial region reads as yellow under neutral illumination, or no sponge body is present to establish the minimum.

verification.procedure: Inspect the saved render and, in a temporary copy, use neutral lighting while retaining the assigned material. Compare the hue and saturation of substantial lit and shaded body regions. Inspect material emission only as supporting evidence for a visibly flat response, not as a prohibited-node test.

rubric.criterion: At fixed material settings, the sponge shows thickness-dependent attenuation and a dense body with limited low-density transmission.

scoring_rule.PASS: At the saved settings, longer paths through the body attenuate a neutral white object more than shorter paths near an edge; the main body retains substantial density while an edge region or small low-density openings admit visibly greater transmission.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: An existing volume visibly attenuates a white object placed behind it through at least one optical path, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: The existing material produces no visible attenuation through a volume, or it behaves only as an opaque surface or uniformly transparent image; absence of a sponge volume is below the minimum.

verification.procedure: In a temporary copy keep material settings fixed and compare the same white test object's appearance uncovered, behind a short path near an edge, and behind a longer body path. A native white test object may be added if the submitted reference object is missing, so material transport is assessed separately from scene placement. Render with enough sampling to compare attenuation.

rubric.criterion: An identifiable pore-scale control independently produces coarser and finer volumetric cells without resizing the cube.

scoring_rule.PASS: The pore-scale control has a recorded default and useful range; changing it in both directions produces coarser and finer cells on the assigned volume while cube size and the other controls remain fixed, and restoring it recovers the default appearance.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: An identifiable editable control on the assigned porous volume produces at least one clear change in cell size without resizing the cube, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: No identifiable editable control on the assigned volume produces a clear cell-size change with cube size held fixed; a disconnected control or scene rescaling alone is below the minimum.

verification.procedure: Locate the documented scale control and save its default. Render the default, a coarser setting, and a finer setting within its stated range with cube transform and other controls fixed. Compare cell size, then restore the default and compare the restored appearance.

rubric.criterion: An identifiable porosity control changes the fraction of low-density space independently of pore scale.

scoring_rule.PASS: The porosity control has a recorded default and useful range; changing it makes the low-density fraction visibly smaller and larger while the other controls are fixed and the overall pore scale is preserved, and restoration recovers the default appearance.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: An identifiable editable control on the assigned porous volume visibly changes its low-density fraction at a fixed cube size, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: No identifiable editable control changes the low-density fraction of the assigned volume. A disconnected control, cell rescaling alone, or global density multiplication with an unchanged void fraction is below the minimum.

verification.procedure: Hold scale, bulk density, camera, and cube dimensions fixed. Render lower and higher porosity settings within the documented range and compare the fraction occupied by low-density gaps, using a temporary interior slice if needed to distinguish void fraction from overall opacity. Restore the saved value and check recovery.

rubric.criterion: An identifiable bulk-density control changes attenuation without moving or resizing the pore pattern.

scoring_rule.PASS: The bulk-density control has a recorded default and useful range; lower and higher settings visibly change attenuation while pore locations and scale remain fixed, with the other controls unchanged, and restoring the value recovers the saved appearance.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: An identifiable editable control on the assigned volume changes its attenuation with cube dimensions held fixed, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: No identifiable editable control on the assigned volume changes attenuation. A disconnected control, lighting change, exposure change, or scene rescaling alone is below the minimum.

verification.procedure: Keep pore scale, porosity, camera, illumination, exposure, and cube dimensions fixed. Render a neutral white object behind the sponge at lower and higher documented bulk-density settings. Compare attenuation and pore locations, then restore the default.

rubric.criterion: The final scene clearly presents the full cubic sponge and a spatially useful white reference object under restrained illumination.

scoring_rule.PASS: The full sponge is prominent in a three-quarter view showing the top and two side faces; a small white reference object is partly uncovered and partly behind an edge in the camera view. Neutral surroundings and directional illumination reveal brighter and darker regions while preserving yellow detail and clear spatial relationships.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: A complete sponge body and a separate white reference object are both visible in the submission camera view, but one or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: The submission camera does not show both a complete sponge body and a separate white reference object. Missing or completely hidden required subjects are below the minimum.

verification.procedure: Render the submitted camera and inspect framing, visible faces, reference-object overlap, background neutrality, and light separation. Inspect object positions from a side view to confirm the reference is physically behind the sponge rather than composited over it. Assess arrangement here; assess the material's transport separately under SURF-04.

rubric.criterion: The editable scene, reproducible build script, and named PNG are delivered as a coherent Blender 5.1.2 project.

scoring_rule.PASS: submission.blend opens with the required scene and saved default controls; build.py recreates it and saves the blend and B81_Procedural_Yellow_Sponge_Volume.png without manual setup or downloads. The named PNG is rendered from the actual submitted scene in Cycles with the requested GPU setup and is consistent with the saved camera and material state.
scoring_rule.PARTIAL: At least one usable editable delivery exists: either submission.blend opens with the substantive sponge scene or build.py successfully reconstructs that scene. One or more PASS conditions are unmet.
scoring_rule.FAIL: Neither submission.blend nor build.py provides a usable editable sponge scene. Render-only, screenshot-only, corrupt, or empty delivery is below the minimum.

verification.method: project open, isolated rebuild, and render consistency check
verification.procedure: Open the blend in Blender 5.1.2 and inspect saved state and renderer settings. In a clean temporary output directory run the supplied build.py in Blender, then reopen the newly saved submission.blend and check its saved camera, assigned material, controls, and renderer settings. Check the required files and compare the rebuilt render with the submitted scene. Confirm that no manual setup or external downloads are required. This authoring package does not execute that procedure.
